affectedPublicSurfaces: `GET /v1/demo/decisions` and `GET /v1/demo/decisions/{id}` (`backend/src/juli_backend/api/routes/demo_decisions.py`) on `api.app-juli.com` — the masked envelope (`_build_masked_item`) gains an executability discriminator that reveals whether Juli can carry a recommendation out, without exposing `workflow_key` or any of the eleven-workflow taxonomy.

`POST /v1/demo/decisions/{id}/approve` on `api.app-juli.com` — `services/agent/approval.py` stops pinning every run to `OPTIMIZE_PRODUCT_PLAYBOOK.workflow_key` regardless of the card's own `workflow_key`; a card whose `workflow_key` has no registered playbook is now refused with a named 409 (no run row, no enqueue, card stays `active`); a card whose `workflow_key` resolves to a registered playbook creates a run bound to that playbook.

`packages/contracts` — the TypeScript mirror of the decisions envelope shape gains the same discriminator field as the Pydantic model, consumed by the `demo.app-juli.com` lane; per the wave lock this must move in the same PR as the Pydantic change or the cross-language contract test fails CI.
No new route, no new HTTP verb, no schema/migration surface — the diff is additive fields on an existing response envelope plus a new named refusal path on an existing write endpoint.

candidateVerificationJourney.restrictedRoute: Pre-merge: pytest (PYTHONPATH pinned to the worktree's backend/src, per the worktree test-import hazard) proves the 409 refusal and the successful-playbook path at the service layer directly (calling approval.py's approve function, not only through the route) — asserting the persisted run's workflow_key/prompt_version, never the OPTIMIZE_PRODUCT_PLAYBOOK constant — plus a schema test on GET /v1/demo/decisions and /v1/demo/decisions/{id} asserting the discriminator is present and workflow_key is still absent, and a cross-tenant/nonexistent-card test asserting both return 404. Post-deploy: authenticated GET /v1/demo/decisions on the candidate port returns the discriminator field on every card; approving a card whose workflow_key has no registered playbook returns 409 with no run created. Post-deploy verification does NOT approve a card that DOES resolve to a registered playbook — that would enqueue a real agent run, and per the wave's owner decision writes stay sandbox-shop-bound and unattempted here; the successful-playbook path is proven pre-merge only.
candidateVerificationJourney.notes: apiSideEffectsInScope is false: the post-deploy journey is a read (GET /v1/demo/decisions) plus one refusal-only write attempt (approve on a non-executable card, which the acceptance criteria require to create no run row and enqueue nothing). workersDisabledOnCandidate is false because no worker path participates in the refusal — the 409 is raised before any enqueue. The card-executes-a-real-playbook path stays proven pre-merge, never exercised as post-deploy candidate traffic, consistent with the wave-wide 'writes stay sandbox-bound' lock.

rollbackAssertion.preCutoverFailureBehavior: Do not merge. Nothing about the deployed system changes until this lands — approval.py continues silently pinning every run to OPTIMIZE_PRODUCT_PLAYBOOK exactly as today, and the decisions envelope continues withholding both workflow_key and the discriminator. No new exposure introduced by this plan; the pre-existing silent-substitution behavior is the known defect this issue fixes, not a regression this plan causes.
rollbackAssertion.postCutoverFailureBehavior: Reverting restores the previous envelope, which is a strict subset of the new one — the issue body states this explicitly. Assert no consumer (apps/demo, packages/contracts) requires the new discriminator field to render before the rollback is considered safe. Reverting also restores approval.py's prior (silent-substitution) dispatch behavior; that regression is the pre-existing state, not a new one, and is acceptable as a rollback target because it is what production runs today.

doNotInfer: The refusal must be proven at the service layer (approval.py) directly, not only through the HTTP route — a future caller must not be able to route around it.

Approve must run the card's OWN playbook when one is registered, never substitute a different one. Today's every-card-runs-Optimize-Product behavior is the defect being removed, not a pattern to preserve for any card.

The discriminator must reveal NO workflow taxonomy — it answers only 'can Juli execute this', never which of the eleven workflows a card belongs to. workflow_key itself stays absent from both envelopes; a schema test must assert that.
The discriminator must be derived from the REAL playbook registry, never a second hand-maintained literal — prove it by registering a fixture playbook and observing the value change.
Cross-tenant and nonexistent cards stay indistinguishable — both 404, never 403, no existence oracle.
The packages/contracts TypeScript mirror moves in the SAME PR as the Pydantic model change, or the cross-language contract test fails CI.

This does not generalize the single-workflow constraint to the other ten workflows — that is explicitly P13/W10. This slice makes today's single-workflow constraint honest (refuse instead of silently substitute); it does not remove it.

Do not approve an executable card against any real shop as part of proving this slice's post-deploy journey — the successful-playbook path is proven pre-merge via the service layer and persisted run columns, consistent with the wave-wide sandbox-bound-writes lock.
